paper.title: Ranked bandits in metric spaces: learning optimally diverse rankings over large document collections

settings.name_in_paper: k-slot ranked bandit problem in metric spaces (conditionally L-continuous user distribution)
unmapped: Action is an ordered list of k documents (k slots); users scan top-down and click the first relevant document (cascade-type feedback)
Objective is fraction of satisfied users (non-abandonment); guarantees are relative to (1-1/e)*OPT or the greedy optimum
User distribution is conditionally L-continuous w.r.t. a known metric: mu(.|Z_S) is Lipschitz for every set S of skipped documents
Bounds depend on covering dimension d of the metric space with constant alpha
settings.definition_quote: Formally, we define the \problem, an instance of which consists of a triple $(X,\D,\P)$, where $(X,\D)$ is a metric space that is known to an algorithm, and $\P$ is a latent user distribution which is conditionally L-continuous w.r.t. $(X,\D)$.

symbols.alpha_cov: constant in the covering-dimension definition N_r(X) <= alpha r^{-d}
symbols.k_slots: number of slots in the ranking
symbols.d_cov: covering dimension of the metric space (X,D)

conditions: user distribution conditionally L-continuous w.r.t. the known metric
metric space has covering dimension d with constant alpha

source.label: thm:regret-RankGridEXP
source.quote: Consider the \problem{} on a metric space with covering dimension $d$ (as defined in~\eqref{eq:dim-defn}, with constant $\alpha$). Then after $T$ rounds $\rankedGridEXP$ achieves \frac{\E[\mathtt{\#clicks}]}{T} \geq (1-\tfrac{1}{e})\,\OPT - \tilde{O}\left( \frac{\alpha k}{T^{1/(d+2)}} \right).

results.notes: Bound on (1-1/e)-approximate regret: (1-1/e)*T*OPT - E[#clicks]; paper states a per-round bound, multiplied by T here. Comparator is the optimal ranking scaled by (1-1/e). Horizon type unclear (GridEXP3 phases are T-independent).

source.label: thm:regret-RankContZoom
source.quote: Consider the \problem{} on a metric space with covering dimension $d$ (as defined in~\eqref{eq:dim-defn}, with constant $\alpha$). Then after $T$ rounds algorithm \rankedContextualZooming{} achieves \frac{\E[\mathtt{\#clicks}]}{T} \geq (1-\tfrac{1}{e})\,\OPT - \tilde{O}\left( \frac{\alpha k}{T^{1/(kd+2)}} \right).

results.notes: (1-1/e)-approximate regret; per-round bound multiplied by T. Zooming confidence radius uses horizon T.

source.label: thm:convergence
source.quote: Fix an instance of the $k$-slot MAB problem. The performance of anytime-\rankedContextualZooming{} up to any given time $t$ is equal to the greedy optimum minus $f(t)$ such that $f(t)\to 0$.

results.notes: Convergence result without rate: time-averaged performance gap to the greedy optimum vanishes. Stated for the metric-less k-slot ranked bandit setting. Encoded as limsup of per-round gap = 0.
